lead.hed: Carrier Eisenhower heads back to Norfolk after losing a Growler in a landing mishap
lead.insight: USS Dwight D. Eisenhower is returning to Naval Station Norfolk after a Sept. 28 landing mishap that cost the Navy an EA-18G Growler and injured four sailors, USNI News reported Saturday. The Navy said the jet, from the Whidbey Island-based “Zappers” of Electronic Attack Squadron 130, had an arresting-gear failure while landing off the Virginia coast. Both aviators ejected and were picked up by search-and-rescue crews from Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron 7. The Navy said the return to port will allow a comprehensive assessment after the mishap. It has not said how long Ike will stay pierside or how the carrier’s training schedule will shift.
lead.image_credit: MC Seaman Melissa Arms Kelly, U.S. Navy · DVIDS 9979984 · Public domain · Ordnance sailors of Strike Fighter Squadron 32 secure gear for sea aboard USS Dwight D. Eisenhower (CVN 69) in the Atlantic, Sept. 29, 2026.

political.hed: Navy signs up to $24.4 billion deal for more than 1,900 SM-6 missiles
political.insight: The five-year award to RTX’s Raytheon, with two option years, covers the Standard Missile-6 used for air defense, ballistic-missile defense and ship strikes. Congress still has to appropriate the money year by year.

political.hed: Saudi Arabia plans an offensive to retake the Red Sea strait from the Houthis
political.insight: Gulf, Yemeni and Western officials told Reuters the Saudi-backed push could come within weeks, led by Yemeni ground forces with Saudi air strikes. The Houthis seized the Bab el-Mandeb strait last month. Officials said more than 100,000 Yemeni troops could be mobilized, and the U.S. is already supplying intelligence.

political.hed: Fraud task force says it is dropping 760,000 unverified enrollees from ACA rolls
political.insight: The administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud says removing the unverified Affordable Care Act enrollees saves $2.2 billion. Heritage calls it another win for the task force; the figures are the government’s own claim.

political.hed: Italy’s coalition moves to cut up to €8 billion from planned defense spending
political.insight: A Cabinet decision Thursday, pushed by Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini, would trim the defense money Italy expected under an EU deficit exemption from about €21 billion to around €14 billion. A government source called the cut agreed but not yet final. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has backed Ukraine and NATO targets, but voters and coalition partners are pulling the other way.

tech.hed: France plans to fly fighters with AI-driven combat drones in 2028
tech.insight: The French Air Force, its armament directorate and the defense AI agency are working on a 2028 flight pairing crewed jets with combat drones under a project called Hypairion. Officials want government-owned, open software for command and mission autonomy.

culture.hed: American Reformer reads Burning Man as a search for a ladder to heaven
culture.insight: Joshua Farris notes that this year’s festival theme, “Axis Mundi,” openly borrows Jacob’s Ladder. He argues the crowds in the Nevada desert are showing a hunger for transcendence that a post-Christian culture has not answered.

culture.hed: Providence covers a women’s convention that drafted a new declaration at Seneca Falls
culture.insight: Nearly 200 women met in Rochester, N.Y., Sept. 17-19 for the 2026 Women’s Convention, ending at Seneca Falls with a declaration of their own. Providence writes on what the gathering proposes for women and the country.
